intro: A bicycle chained to a post. Tires flat, chain good.

text: Chain, gears, cables. All of it useful.
The bolts are fused. Got a sore wrist, nothing else.

options.label: Pump the tires and ride it a while

text: Flew down three blocks. Felt like being twelve.
Front tire burst. Walked it back to where I started.

intro: Crows. Hundreds, on every wire, all watching me.

text: They lost interest. One followed me for a block, though.
They all took off at once. The noise. Anything nearby heard it.
Not one moved. I don't like that either.
They dove. Pecked my neck and scalp. Just scratches.

intro: A shopping cart on its side, full of pill bottles. Labels faded.

options.label: Sort them, read what you can

text: Antibiotics and painkillers. The real thing.
Can't read half of them. Took nothing: not worth the risk.
Something in here will be useful. Probably.
Vitamins. All vitamins. Great.

intro: Clean laundry on a line between two balconies. Someone hung it recently.

options.label: Call out to whoever lives here

text: An old man waves from the window. Trades me a jar of beans for news.
A door slams. Then silence. Then a dog, inside, very big.

options.label: Leave it alone and move on

text: Somebody's still living here. That's... good. I think.
Felt eyes on my back for two blocks.

intro: A school bus, doors open, backpacks still on the seats.

text: Snacks, a flashlight, batteries. And a drawing I folded into my pocket.
Just notebooks. I couldn't stop reading the names.
The battery's dead but the alternator's fine. Coming with me.
Engine's been stripped already.
Some places you just don't go in.
I went in anyway in my head. All day.

intro: A dog, skinny, wagging. It wants to follow me.

text: It ate and walked beside me a while. Then it barked at a doorway: someone had stashed cans there.
success.memory: the dog that walked with me

text: It ate and ran off. Fair.
It left. Looked back twice.
It kept following and barking. Had to hide.

intro: The footbridge is down. The river underneath is low, but fast.

text: Soaked to the waist, but across.
The current took my feet. Banged my knee on a rock.

options.label: Walk upstream to the next bridge

text: Long way. Found a dry crossing.
The next bridge was down too. Back to the start.

options.label: Rig a line from the wreckage

text: Took a while, but the line held. I'll leave it for next time.
The line slipped. Gave up and walked around.

intro: An old army checkpoint. Sandbags, a barrier, nobody. A rifle rack, empty.

text: Radio batteries and a logbook. Last entry: 'they're not coming back for us'.
Rats. Nothing but rats.
Nothing. Kept going.
Tripped a can-alarm. Hid for twenty minutes.

intro: The stairwell is pitch black. Something drips, far above.

text: Just water. A whole floor of storage at the top.
The light caught something on the landing. It moved. I didn't stay.

options.label: Climb in the dark, by touch

text: Quiet all the way up. Found a stash by feel.
Missed a step. Twisted my ankle.

intro: A lone trader with a handcart. Wants batteries, offers food.

text: A fair deal. She even threw in a tip about the road ahead.
She short-changed me and I noticed too late.
Got the better end. She laughed about it. I liked her.
She packed up and left. No deal.
Nodded and moved on.
She followed a while, asking. Annoying.

intro: A rooftop greenhouse. Most of it dead. Some tomatoes, gone wild.

text: Small, sour, real tomatoes. I almost cried.
All rotten under the leaves.
Seeds in a twist of paper. Someone at home will know what to do.
success.memory: seeds from the rooftop greenhouse

text: Dropped them through a crack in the floor.

intro: I bumped a car and its alarm went off. After all these years.

options.label: Pop the hood and kill it

text: Silenced. And look: a battery that still works.
Couldn't find the wire. It screamed for a full minute.
Two blocks away, under a truck. Nothing came.
Something came. I didn't see it. I heard it sniffing.

intro: A supermarket. The front's been looted to the floor. The loading bay hasn't.

text: Crates. Real ones. Flour gone hard, but cans.
Pulled something in my back.
Things roll under shelves. Three cans and a lighter.
Glass and mouse droppings.

intro: A body against a wall, long gone. A note pinned to the jacket.

text: 'Tell Ana I tried.' And a key taped underneath. It opened a locker nearby.
success.memory: the note that said 'tell Ana I tried'

text: I couldn't. I just couldn't.
Put my coat over the face. It felt right.
Couldn't look away for a long time.

intro: Hail. Sudden, hard, the size of marbles.

text: Waited it out in a bus stop. Ice everywhere after.
The roof I picked leaked. Soaked and cold.
Ugly, but I made good time.
Got hit in the head. Seeing stars.

intro: A gas station. The lights are on. Somebody's got a generator here.

text: A woman with a shotgun and a kind face. Gave me water and a tip.
A shot over my head. I left fast.
Her spare fuel cans. I took one. I'm not proud.
A dog. A big dog. I ran.
Not my business.
Longer way around than I thought.

intro: A cell tower, with a maintenance cabinet at the base.

text: Circuit boards, good copper, a backup battery.
Shocked myself. Some cell's still charged.

options.label: Climb a few meters to look around

text: Saw the whole district from up there. Easier route back.
Froze halfway. Came down slow.

intro: Chalk on the sidewalk: a hopscotch, and an arrow, fresh. 'FOOD →'

text: A little cache in a mailbox. Someone's leaving it for strangers.
The arrow led to an empty lot. Then I found another arrow pointing back at me.
Arrows lead places. I'm not going to that place.
I'll wonder about it all night.

intro: The mall's escalator is stopped, and something's moving at the top of it.

text: A family of foxes. They left. I took the stairs.
Whatever it was came down. I left through the cinema.
Foxes. They scattered. The electronics shop up there was untouched.
It wasn't foxes. I ran. It didn't follow. Yet.

intro: Far off, a train horn. There are no trains.

text: An old horn on a timer, on a pole. Wired to a car battery. Mine now.
Walked toward it for an hour. It kept being far away.
Whatever it is, it can blow its horn without me.
It blew again. Closer.

intro: The underpass is flooded knee-deep. The road beyond is the fast way.

text: Cold and disgusting. Fast.
Something brushed my leg. I sprinted the rest.

options.label: Go over the top, along the railings

text: Balanced the whole way. Dry feet.
Slipped and went in anyway.
Long. Boring. Dry.
Long, boring and it rained.

intro: A farmhouse with smoke from the chimney. Chickens in the yard.

text: Eggs! Real eggs. They asked about the radio. I told them how to find you.
Nobody answered. The chickens stared at me.
Got one. I'm a terrible person. A fed terrible person.
Farmer with a pitchfork. I'm faster. Barely.

intro: A small wind turbine on a farm, still spinning.

text: Charge controller, intact. The workshop will love this.
Wrong panel. Spent an hour on nothing.

options.label: Hook up the batteries you carry and wait

text: Charged everything I had. Slow, but free.
The wiring's fried. Waited for nothing.

intro: A pileup across all lanes of the highway. Dozens of cars.

text: Spare parts, a first aid kit, canned food. Somebody was ready.
Already picked clean. Long ago.
Car roofs all the way across. Quick.
Fell between two cars.

intro: At dusk, lights on a hill. Lots of them. Like a town.

text: Candles in jars, on graves. Hundreds. Someone tends them.
success.memory: the hill of candles

text: Someone was waiting by the lights. He saw me.

options.label: Mark it on the map and move on

text: Marked. The radio will want to know about this.
Lost the bearing in the dark.

intro: The road is too quiet. No birds. No wind.

text: There. A voice, far off. Someone singing. Then the birds came back.
Something, far behind me, stopped walking when I stopped.
Got through. Didn't look back.
Ran out of breath halfway. The quiet waited.

intro: A rooftop pigeon coop. A few birds still live there.

text: Four eggs, wrapped in my scarf. Careful now.
Broke them all climbing down.

options.label: There's a band on one bird's leg

text: A message: coordinates and 'supplies, take what you need'.
success.memory: the message on the pigeon's leg

text: Couldn't catch it.

intro: A hospital bed in the middle of the street. Clean sheets. Nobody around.

text: A medkit, tucked in neatly. Like a gift.
Under the sheets: nothing. On the pillow: my name.
Walked around it. Wide.
When I looked back, the sheets were folded down.

intro: A storm drain grate, pried open. Rungs go down into the dark.

text: Someone's old hideout. Blankets, cans, a camp stove.
Water rushing somewhere below. I lost my footing.

options.label: Put the grate back and mark it

text: Covered. Whatever's down there, stays there.
Too heavy. Left it open.

intro: A storm on the horizon, but it's not rain. The radio's screaming. Hair standing up on my arms.

options.label: Dig in and wait it out

text: Lay flat in a ditch for an hour. Lightning walked right past us.
Waited too long in the open. Something hit near enough to throw me.

options.label: Outrun it to the next ridge

text: Made the ridge. Looking back, the ground where we were is black glass.
It caught us halfway. I don't remember the next part.

intro: A convoy, twenty trucks, parked nose to tail. Doors open. Nobody. Engines still have fuel.

text: Hose, can, patience. Got a good haul.
Fumes. Threw up twice, got nothing.
Glove boxes. Tools, a first-aid tin, a map with circles on it.
Something was living in the last cab. It didn't want me there.

options.label: Leave it. It feels like bait

text: We went around. Later we saw the smoke from a fire where the convoy was.
Leaving it bothered me all night.

intro: Footprints in the dust, fresh. Lots of them, barefoot, going exactly where we're going.

text: A camp. Whoever they are, they left a cache under a stone. We took half.
They knew we were following. They waited for us.
Hours lost. Nothing followed us.
The long way had its own problems.

intro: A hatch in the ground, like ours. Somebody's knocking from inside. Three, then two.

text: An old man and a lot of tins. He gave us some and asked us to tell nobody where he is.
It was a trap, or a madman. Hard to tell which.
We talked for an hour. He sent up a bag on a rope: batteries, and a list of frequencies.
He stopped answering. The knocking went on, though.

intro: Lights out on the plain at night. Moving. Not cars. They stop when we stop.

options.label: Kill the lamp and stay still

text: They went past at dawn. I'm not going to describe them.
I couldn't stay still. They noticed.
They flashed back. Morse. Coordinates. A cache, right where they said.
They came closer. Much closer.

intro: An abandoned workshop on the road. A car on the lift, half fixed. The tools are still on the wall.

text: Took what fits in a bag. The good stuff.
Dropped the engine block on my foot. Mostly my boot.
Slept under a roof for the first time in days. Feel human.
Couldn't sleep. Kept hearing the lift creak.

intro: A mall, flooded to the second floor. The third floor's dry. The escalator's under water.

text: Cold. So cold. But the pharmacy up there is untouched.
Something brushed my leg down there. I came up too fast and hit my head.
Up the drainpipe, in a window. Clothes, tins, batteries.
The drainpipe came off the wall.

intro: A ferry, run aground, tilted. The fuel tanks are on the low side, half under the water.

text: Rigged a pump out of a bike wheel. Filled every can we had.
The hull shifted while I was inside.
Charts, a flare gun, the captain's medical kit.
Just gulls and the smell.

intro: Out on the white, a town. Houses, a church, a water tower. It wasn't there an hour ago.

text: We kept walking. When I looked back it was gone.
I kept looking back. It kept being there.
It's real. A real town, a real well, real people who don't want visitors. They traded.
We walked for hours. It never got closer.

intro: A plane, belly down on the salt. Cargo door open. Crates.

text: Medical supplies. Military. Enough to fill everything we carry.
The crates were nailed. One gave way all at once.
The radio still works. I said our call sign. Somebody, very far away, said it back.
Somebody was already in the cockpit. Still is.

intro: The observatory dome. Inside, a desk with a logbook. The last entry is today's date.

text: Frequencies. Times. A list of names, and ours is on it. Took the book.
The pages are blank except the last one. It says: LEAVE.
A whole room of batteries, still charged. We took what we could carry.
Found it. It was running. Something was feeding it.

intro: The big dish is turning. The control room door is open. A chair is still warm.

text: Pointed it at home. For a second I heard the bunker on it, clear as anything.
Sparks. The whole panel went up. We ran.

options.label: Hide and see who comes back

text: Nobody came back. Nobody at all. We took the spares off the shelf and left.
Somebody came back.

intro: A woman at a stall waves me over. "For you, a special price." She says that to everyone.

text: Talked her down to half. She laughed and threw in a tin.
She talked me up instead. I don't know how.
Heard where a stall keeps its spare batteries. Good to know.
Too many people. Too loud. I left early.

intro: A kid bumps into me in the crowd. Says sorry. Too polite.

text: Got my chips back, and the kid's. Gave the kid's back. Mostly.
Slipped right out of my hand. Gone, with my chips.
Not worth a fight in front of the guards. Felt good, letting it go.
It's eating at me.

intro: On the way out, two men fall in behind me. They stop when I stop.

text: Through a tent, under a tarp, gone.
They cornered me behind the carousel. Took a cut of what I was carrying.
They decided I wasn't worth it.
I was right and they were bigger.
The guards walked me to the road. Didn't even ask for chips.
The guards were on a break. Of course.

intro: An old man repairs radios at a stall in the back. Soldering iron, magnifying glass, a sign: NO PROMISES.

text: He put the iron down. Talked for an hour. About a network, about a night, about what it heard.
He pretended not to hear. Come back another day, maybe.
Two drinks in he was drawing diagrams on a napkin. I kept the napkin.
He drank it and went back to work. Fair enough.

intro: Down in the dam's control room, behind a door marked AUTHORISED ONLY, something is humming.

text: A steel cabinet with ECHO stencilled on it. Still running. There's a logbook.
The door won. My shoulder lost.
Click. Inside: a cabinet marked ECHO, humming, and a logbook nobody finished.
Broke the pick in it. Someone will have to come back.

intro: The observatory's console room. Every screen is dark except one, showing a single point in the sky.

options.label: Read what's taped to the console

text: Numbers. The Voice's numbers. Written as coordinates. And a note.
My hands were shaking too much to read it. We'll come back.
Copied it all, line by line, with the dish turning overhead.
The dish moved. I ran. I'm not ashamed.

intro: Storm's right on top of me. Lightning just hit a lamppost down the block.
Hair's standing up on my arms. I need to decide fast.

options.label: Get into a doorway and wait it out

text: Squeezed into a doorway. Counted the thunder. It moved on.
Doorway was half collapsed. Got soaked and rattled anyway.
Ran it bent double. Made the next block before the worst of it.
A gust threw me into a fence. I'm up. I'm fine. Mostly.

options.label: Use it: nobody's watching the depot in this

text: Walked right into the depot under the noise. Nobody. Took what I could carry.
Someone was sheltering there too. We both ran. I ran faster, but empty-handed.

intro: Storm's getting worse. There's a city bus on its side across the avenue.
Could wait it out in there.

text: Sat in the bus listening to the rain hammer the roof. Weirdly peaceful.
success.memory: waiting out the storm in a toppled bus

text: Every bang on the roof made me jump. Didn't rest at all.

options.label: Strip the dashboard radio while you're in there

text: Pried the radio out of the dash. Speaker, wiring, a fuse box. All good.
Cut my hand on the panel. Got nothing out but blood.
Head down, kept going. Wet, but on schedule.
Slipped in the gutter. Lost my footing and my nerve.

intro: Lightning's hitting the antenna mast over and over. Every strike, my radio screams.
Between strikes there's... a voice. Not ours. Reading numbers.

options.label: Stay and listen between the strikes

text: Wrote the numbers on my arm. Coordinates, I think. There was a cache under the mast's base.
success.memory: the numbers between lightning strikes

text: Too much noise. And then the voice said my name. I left.
Backed off a hundred meters. The voice stopped when I did. Don't like that.
Couldn't make my legs move for a minute. Then I could.

intro: Rain's flooded the underpass. Waist-deep, brown water, things floating in it.

text: Cold. Disgusting. Done.
Stepped in a hole and went under. Swallowed some. I'll live.
Long way round. Dry socks. Worth it.
Long way round, and it was flooded too. Great.

options.label: Float a door across and fish out the crates

text: Rode a door across like a raft. Hooked two crates on the way.
The door flipped. I swam. The crates swam away.

intro: The rain's washing everything out of the gutters and drains. Stuff's piling up at the grate.

options.label: Sift through what the rain brings

text: Bolts, a battery, a ring of keys. The rain does the digging for you.
Mostly leaves and someone's shoe. Wet for nothing.

options.label: Set out cans to catch the rainwater

text: Drank till I sloshed. Filled the bottles. Small things.
Cans kept tipping over in the wind. Gave up.

intro: Fog's so thick I can't see my feet. And there are voices in it. Talking, laughing.
Like a party. Somewhere close.

text: Followed it. A tape recorder on a windowsill, looping a party from years ago. Took the batteries. Left the tape.
success.memory: the party on tape in the fog

text: The voices stopped when I moved. All at once. I'm getting out of here.
A woman called back. Traders, waiting out the fog. They shared a can and a rumour.
They weren't friendly. I ran into the white and lost them. And myself, for a while.
Slid past like I wasn't there. Never found out who they were.
Kicked a can. The voices went silent. Then I ran.

intro: There's something big in the fog. Breathing.
...It's a horse. A real horse, standing in the middle of the road.

text: It let me touch its nose. Warm. It walked with me to the edge of the fog and then stayed.
success.memory: the horse in the fog that let me touch it

text: It shied and bolted. Felt its hooves through the ground.
Got on. Held on. It knew where it was going, and so did I, for once. Fastest I've moved in years.
success.memory: riding a horse out of the fog

text: It threw me. Hard.
Left it to the fog. Some things should stay free.
Left it. Felt bad about it for a block.

intro: It's dark. There's a candle in a window, third floor. Someone lives there.

options.label: Knock and say who you are

text: An old woman with a shotgun. Then with tea. She gave me something 'for the young ones at the radio'.
success.memory: the old woman with the candle and the tea

text: The candle went out. A voice said to leave. I left.

options.label: Watch the window from the dark

text: Saw them hide a sack under the stairs before bed. I could take it. I didn't. But now I know they're there.
A dog started barking. Had to move on.
Walked on. Nice to know someone else keeps a light on.
Walked on. Kept looking back at it.

intro: Clear night out here. More stars than I've ever seen in this city.
Without the lights, you can see all of them.

options.label: Stop a while and look up

text: Lay on a car roof for ten minutes. Found the Southern Cross. Felt small, in a good way.
success.memory: the night I lay on a car roof under the stars

text: Couldn't relax. Too exposed. Kept going.

options.label: Climb the water tower for a look around

text: From the top, I could see a lit window far east. Someone's out there. Felt less alone.
The ladder rung snapped. Caught myself. Heart's still going.

options.label: Use the moonlight to cover ground

text: Moved fast and quiet. Bright enough to see, dark enough to hide.
Too bright. Felt watched the whole way.

intro: Flat grey light, no shadows. Perfect for reading tracks in the dust.
Someone's been dragging something heavy along here. Recently.

text: Into a garage, under a tarp: somebody's stash. They haven't been back in a while.
Lost them on the asphalt. Wasted half an hour.
Took the other street. Never saw them.
Took the other street. Heard dragging behind me the whole way.

intro: Sun's out. There's a solar panel on this roof, and it's still humming.

options.label: Unbolt it and pull the cells

text: Two cells came out clean, and the charge controller.
Cracked it getting it off. Glass everywhere.

options.label: Leave it, but charge the radio off it

text: Hooked the radio up for twenty minutes. Clearest signal all trip.
Wrong polarity. Smelled something burn. Radio's okay. I think.

intro: Under a collapsed awning... a racing bike frame. Proper one, the kind that cost a fortune.
No wheels, no chain. But the frame's light as a feather.

options.label: Ease it out from under the rubble

text: Took my time. It's out, and it's straight. Strapping it to my pack.
The awning shifted and pinned it. I'll have to leave it.
Came free with a scream of metal. Not a scratch. Bringing it home.
Pulled too hard. The awning came down on my shoulder.
Left it. Probably smart.
Left it. Already regretting it.

intro: A bike shop with the shutter half up. Most of it's stripped.
But up on the wall hooks: a pair of thin racing wheels. Nobody could reach them.

text: Crates held. Got both wheels down, spokes and all.
Crates didn't hold.

options.label: Fish them down with a pole

text: Ten minutes with a curtain rod and a lot of swearing. Got them.
Knocked one down; it bent on the counter. Not worth it now.

options.label: Forget the wheels, check the back shelves

text: Inner tubes, patches, a pump. Useful bits.
Empty. Someone beat me to the back.

intro: In a locker at the back: a rag wrapped round something, oiled and careful.
It's a full chain and gear set. Someone was saving this.

options.label: Take it, wrapped as it is

text: Whoever wrapped it isn't coming back for it. I'll take care of it like they did.
Hands were shaking. Dropped it, scattered half the bits. Got most of them.

options.label: Check the locker for a name first

text: A name tag: 'TOMÁS — DON'T TOUCH'. Sorry, Tomás. Thank you, Tomás.
success.memory: Tomás and his careful chain

text: No name. Took it anyway.

intro: There's a motorbike under a tarp in the service hangar. Big old single-cylinder.
Engine looks seized, but it's whole. That's rare.

options.label: Unbolt the engine and drag it out

text: Four hours of bolts and swearing. The engine's on a cart. I'm walking it home.
Stripped two bolts. It's not coming out today.

options.label: Too heavy. Strip what you can

text: Plugs, cables, a carb gasket. Better than nothing.
Even the small stuff's rusted solid.

intro: Behind the building, half under a tarp: a police sidecar. Just the sidecar, the bike's long gone.
Dented, but the frame's sound. Seat's even still padded.

options.label: Roll it out and push it home

text: It has a wheel. A squeaky, wobbly wheel. Pushing it all the way.
The wheel came off at the first curb. Had to leave it.
Nobody around. Rolled it out the back gate quiet as anything.
Someone was living in it. I backed off.

intro: A motorbike wreck in a ditch, picked over. But the tank's untouched.
And the carburetor's still bolted on. Clean inside.

options.label: Take tank and carburetor together, carefully

text: Drained the dregs, wrapped the carb in my shirt. Both coming home.
Cracked the carb bowl. The tank alone isn't worth the weight.

options.label: Just siphon the fuel and go

text: A couple of liters. Not nothing.
Mostly water in there.

intro: A bike leaning on a fence. Tires pumped, chain oiled. It works.
There's a lock on it. And a note taped to the seat: 'BACK SOON'.

options.label: Cut the lock and ride it home

text: Lock gave. Riding home. Whoever 'back soon' was, they weren't.
Bolt cutters slipped. Lock held. Hand didn't.
Lock popped. Took the bike. Left the note.
Twenty minutes on the lock. Nothing.
Left it. Wrote 'GOOD LUCK' under 'BACK SOON'. Felt right.
Left it. Kept thinking about it the whole way.

intro: That fence again, where the bike was. The bike's gone.
But there's a different one here now. And a new note: 'FOR WHOEVER WROTE GOOD LUCK. WE MADE IT. THIS ONE'S SPARE.'

text: Tears in my eyes on a stranger's bike. Riding home.
success.memory: the spare bike a stranger left for us

text: Took it. Couldn't stop grinning.

options.label: Leave it for someone who needs it more

text: Left it there with a new note: 'PASS IT ON'. Walking home lighter anyway.
success.memory: the bike I passed on

text: Left it. Hope that was right.

intro: An old man sitting in a newspaper kiosk like nothing happened. Shotgun across his knees.
He says he's guarding his stock. There isn't much. He looks hungry.

text: He ate slowly. Told me about the neighbourhood before. Said to come back sometime.
success.memory: the old man in the kiosk I shared food with

text: He wouldn't take it. Pride. But he nodded at me like I'd done something.

options.label: Ask what he's seen around here

text: He knew every stash in four blocks. Told me one.
He talked for half an hour about his cat. Nothing useful.

options.label: Take his stock. He can't stop you

text: He didn't fight. That was worse. Got cans and a bit of medicine.
He fired. Missed, mostly.

intro: The old man's kiosk. Shutter's half up, nobody inside.
There's a box on the counter with a note: 'FOR THE RADIO PEOPLE. YOU KNOW WHO.'

text: Batteries, medicine, a bag of honey drops, and a drawing of a cat. He kept the best for us.
success.memory: the box the old man left for the radio people

text: Batteries and medicine. And a drawing of a cat.
Took the box, left a fixed lamp on the counter. Fair's fair.
success.memory: the lamp I left for the old man

text: Tried to fix his lamp. Didn't. Took the box anyway.

intro: The kiosk burned. Just a black frame now.
No sign of the old man.

text: A few melted cans. A shotgun with no stock. I keep thinking about him.
Nothing. Just ash.
Kept walking. Didn't look back.
Kept walking. Looked back anyway.

intro: Wait. That dog. The skinny one. It's not skinny anymore, and it found me.
It's pulling at my sleeve. It wants me to follow.

text: Led me through a hole in a wall to a cellar. Someone's whole winter stash. It sat and wagged like it was proud.
success.memory: the dog that remembered me and paid me back

text: Lost it in the rubble. It came back later, empty-mouthed and sorry.
Ten minutes with a dog's head on my knee. Best ten minutes in months.
success.memory: the dog's head on my knee

text: It licked my face and ran off. Fine. Still counts.

intro: A man pinned under a fallen shelf. Alive. He's begging me to help.

text: Heaved it off him. He couldn't stop thanking me. Said he'd remember the face.
success.memory: the man under the shelf I pulled out

text: Couldn't shift it alone. Wedged a bar under it and he crawled out. Took ages.

options.label: Wedge it and patch him up first

text: Splinted his leg, wedged the shelf, got him out. He'll walk again.
success.memory: the stranger whose leg I splinted

text: Did what I could. He's out. Not sure he'll make it.

options.label: It might be a trap. Leave him

text: Walked away. Maybe it was a trap. Probably it wasn't.
His voice followed me down three streets.

intro: Someone's whistling from a rooftop. It's the man from under the shelf. Limping, smiling.
He's throwing something down to me.

text: Binoculars. Good ones. 'Watch your back out here,' he says, and he's gone.
success.memory: the binoculars the man from the shelf threw me

text: Fumbled it. It bounced off a car. Still works, mostly.

options.label: Call up and ask how he's doing

text: He's doing fine. Walks with a stick. He tells me where his old crew kept their stores.
He waves, and is gone over the roofs.

intro: There's a hum coming from the substation. Low. I can feel it in my teeth.
The grid's been dead for years.

text: The gate's open. Like someone expected me.
Got as far as the gate. My legs wouldn't. I'm sorry.

options.label: Mark it on the map and walk away

text: Marked it. Didn't look back. Could still hear it two blocks on.
Walked away. Took the long way round, just to not pass it again.

intro: Transformers are cold. Still humming. In the middle of the floor, a chair facing the wall.
And a radio on the chair. It's playing our frequency. It's playing YOU. Something you said yesterday.

options.label: Pull the batteries out of that thing

text: Silence. Real silence. It was a recorder, wired to the antenna on the roof. Someone's been listening to us.
success.memory: the radio in the substation that had our voices on it

text: The door slammed behind me the second I touched it.

options.label: Listen to what else it recorded

text: Days of us. Then other voices, other bunkers, all saying the same things we say.
Then the tape runs out and the hum gets louder. I'm leaving.
success.memory: hearing other bunkers on the tape, saying our words

text: The hum got into my head. I don't remember walking out. I'm outside now. I think.
Out. Didn't turn my back on the chair. Don't ask me why.
Backed into a cabinet. The radio stopped playing. Then it said my name.

intro: Door's stuck. The hum's coming from under the floor now. It's getting louder.
There's a window, high up. And a hatch in the floor.

options.label: Climb out the window, whatever it takes

text: Cut my hands on the glass. Don't care. I'm out. I'm out.
The frame gave. I fell wrong.

options.label: Open the hatch and face it

text: Stairs. A generator room. Running. Someone's been feeding it diesel. Recently.
Took their spare can. If they want it back, they know where to find us. That's the problem.
success.memory: the generator under the substation that someone keeps fed

text: It was dark down there. Something was breathing in the dark.

options.label: Sit tight and wait for the hum to stop

text: It stopped at dawn. So did the lock. Walked out like nothing. Nothing was fine.
It didn't stop. It never stopped. I kicked the door until it gave.

intro: A church bell. Ringing in the fog. Slow, like a funeral.
Nobody's rung a bell in this city in years.

text: Found the church. The doors are open. The bell stopped when I stepped in.
Lost it in the fog. It kept ringing from the other side of me. Every side.

options.label: Stay put and count the rings

text: Eleven. Then nothing. Eleven. Like the last time I heard it. I never heard it before.
success.memory: the bell in the fog that rang eleven

text: Lost count. Started again. Lost count. I'm moving on.
Went the other way. Fog's thinner there. Good.
Every way I went, the bell was ahead of me.

intro: The bell rope's tied to a clock motor. Somebody set this up.
And the pews. Coats on every pew, folded. Each one with a paper tag. Names.

text: Strangers. Strangers. Then a tag with my name on it. My handwriting.
I didn't write it. I didn't.
success.memory: the coat in the church with my name on it

text: Too dark to read. I didn't want to anyway.
Candles, wine, a first-aid box nobody opened. Someone keeps this place.
The sacristy door opened from the inside before I touched it. I ran.
Warm. Fits. Pocket had a candy and a note: 'for the walk home'.
Put it on and it was wet. Inside. Took it off. My shirt is wet now too.

intro: Knocking. Under a manhole. Three, two, three.
Somebody's down there.

text: It's heavy. Got it. A girl's face looking up. Fifteen, maybe. She doesn't scream.
Couldn't shift it. The knocking stopped. I told myself she found another way out.
Three, two, three. A pause. Then she pushes from below and I pull. A girl. Thin.
Knocked. Silence. Knocked again. Nothing. Maybe I scared them.
Walked on. The knocking followed me for a block.
Walked on. I can still hear it. I'll hear it tonight.

intro: Her name's Abril. Been in the drains since the water came up. Days.
She's got a ring of keys she won't let go of.

text: She ate like it was a crime. Then she gave me the keys.
"The pharmacy on the corner. The back room. I couldn't go alone."
She took it and ran. Kept the keys. Can't blame her.

options.label: Tell her how to find the bunker

text: Drew her the way on her arm with a pen. She read it three times.
She said she'd think about it. She gave me one key. 'For trusting me.'
She laughed. 'Underground? I've had enough of underground.' Then she was gone.
She looked at me a long time. Then handed them over. I hope I'm what she thinks.
She bolted. Back into the drain. I shouldn't have asked like that.

intro: The pharmacy. The back room's locked tight. Keys fit.
Shelves. Full shelves. But the floor in front of them is wired. A tripwire, old.

text: Over. Filled the bag. Over again. Didn't breathe once, I think.
success.memory: the pharmacy Abril gave us the keys to

text: Caught it with my heel. Shelf came down on my shoulder.
A shotgun shell in a pipe. Took it apart. Took everything. Took the shell too.
It went off. Missed me by a hand. My ears are ringing.

options.label: Grab what's near the door and go

text: Two boxes from the shelf by the door. Enough. Not worth dying for more.
Grabbed a box. It was empty. Someone got here before the wire did.

intro: Writing on a wall in fresh chalk. 'RADIO PEOPLE.' An arrow.
Signed with a drawing of a key.

text: Arrow after arrow. A boarded-up kiosk with a bag inside. A note: 'from the drain. A.'
She made it.
success.memory: the chalk arrows Abril left for us

text: Lost the arrows where someone washed the wall. Found her bag anyway, by luck. Half of it.

options.label: Leave it. It might not be for us

text: Left it. Drew a little radio next to the key, so she knows we saw it.
Left it. Felt wrong all the way.

intro: Dogs. Not one. Seven, eight. Thin. They've been walking behind me for a while.
They stop when I stop.

options.label: Throw them food and back off

text: They went for it. Fought over it. I walked, didn't run. You never run.
They ate it and kept following. Closer now.

options.label: Get up on a car roof

text: Up on a bus. They circled for an hour and lost interest. Lost the hour too.
Slipped on the bonnet. They're on me. Running.
Ran. Found a door. Shut it. They howled at it for a while.
Ran. Wrong street. Dead end.

intro: Cornered. A stairwell. They're at the bottom. Growling now.
There's a fire extinguisher. And a door at the top. Locked.

text: White cloud. They scattered, yelping. I was down and gone before it cleared.
It was empty. Just a cough of powder. They came up.

options.label: Break the door at the top

text: Shoulder, shoulder, shoulder. It gave. Shut it behind me. Hands won't stop shaking.
It wouldn't give. One got my leg before I kicked it off.

options.label: Light a fire on the stairs

text: Paper, a chair, the fuel I had. They backed off from the flames. I went out the window.
Couldn't get it going. Wet. I'm waiting them out, on the top step.

intro: A man on the bridge. Outside the railing. Looking down at the river.
He hasn't seen me yet.

text: He saw me. He didn't move. He said 'don't'. But he's listening.
He saw me and stepped back to the edge. I stopped. I stayed where I was.
Walked on. Didn't look back. I will think about this.
success.memory: the man on the bridge I walked past

text: Walked on. Heard nothing. That's worse.
failure.memory: the man on the bridge I walked past

intro: He asks me why. Why bother. Everyone's gone.
He wants an answer. A real one.

options.label: Tell him about the bunker. About us

text: Told him about the radio. About you. That someone's still keeping the lights on.
He climbed back over. Gave me his compass. 'You'll need it more.'
success.memory: the man I talked down from the bridge

text: He listened. He said thank you. Then he looked at the water for a long time.
I don't know what he did after I left. I keep telling myself.

options.label: Sit on the railing beside him and say nothing

text: We sat. An hour. Then he said 'my legs are cold' and climbed back. We laughed. God.
He said he'd keep an eye out for us.
success.memory: the hour on the bridge

text: We sat. He said 'thank you for sitting'. I looked away for a second.

options.label: Grab him and pull him over

text: Got him by the collar. We both fell on the right side. He punched me. Then he cried.
success.memory: pulling the man off the bridge

text: He fought. We both went over the rail. The cold. I got out. I got out.

intro: Someone on a rooftop. Waving. Both arms.
It's him. The man from the bridge. He's got a garden up there.

text: Tomatoes. On a roof. He wouldn't let me leave without a bag.
He said 'I'm glad you were stupid that day'.
success.memory: the rooftop garden of the man from the bridge

text: Stairs were blocked. He lowered a bucket on a rope instead.
Waved. He waved until I turned the corner.
Waved. He waved until I turned the corner.

intro: Footsteps behind me. Same pace as mine.
I stopped. They stopped. One step late.

text: Turned. Nobody. Street's empty all the way back. But there are footprints in the dust.
Couldn't make myself turn. Walked faster. They walked faster.

options.label: Duck into a doorway and wait

text: Waited ten minutes. Nothing passed. Then I heard it walk away. The other way.
Waited. The steps came right up to the doorway. And stopped. I didn't breathe.
Walked till the steps were gone. Don't know when they stopped.
Faster and faster. So did they. I'm running now.

intro: The footprints. They come up to where I stood.
Then they keep going. Past me. Ahead. Toward an open manhole.

text: Down the ladder. A dry tunnel. Someone's camp, long cold. A tin box.
There were footprints going down. None coming back up.
success.memory: the footprints that walked ahead of me

text: A rung was missing. I fell in the dark.

options.label: Scuff them out and go another way

text: Scuffed out every one. Went around the long way. Felt silly. Didn't feel silly.
Scuffed them out. Behind me, I heard a new one land in the dust.
Nobody answered. Then, from the manhole, very quietly, my own voice: 'who's there?'
success.memory: my voice coming back out of the manhole

text: Nobody answered. I'm going. I'm going now.

intro: Rain's pouring into the subway entrance. But there's light down there.
Electric light.

text: A train at the platform. Lights on. Doors open. No driver.
Halfway down the steps the light went off. Back up. Fast.
Kept to the street. Rain's bad enough.
Kept to the street. The light stayed on behind me. Like it was waiting.

intro: The carriage lights hum. Seats, bags, an umbrella. Like everyone just stood up.
Water's coming in at the far end of the platform.

text: Bags full of somebody's life. Took what's useful. Left the photos.
The doors closed behind me. With a chime. The train's moving.
A battery bank keeps it lit. Pulled half of it. Lights dimmed. Better that way.
Touched the panel. Sparks, water, my arm went dead for a minute.

options.label: Get out before the water does

text: Up the stairs. The lights went off behind me as I reached the street.
Up the stairs. Took one look back. Someone was sitting in the carriage now.

intro: It stopped in the tunnel. Lights off. Water's coming in under the doors.
Up to my ankles. Rising.

text: Got them open. Waded back along the rails in the dark. Never been so glad to see rain.
They wouldn't. The water kept coming.
Emergency hatch. Out on the roof, crawled to a service door. Out.
Couldn't find it in the dark. Found it in the end. Swallowed half the tunnel.

options.label: Climb on the seats and wait

text: It stopped rising at my knees. Then it drained. Walked out at dawn.
It rose past the seats. I swam for the light.

intro: A radio mast on a hill. A cabin at the foot of it. Lamp in the window.
Someone's keeping a light on out here.

text: No answer. Door's open. Lamp's warm. Kettle's warm.
Knocked. The lamp went out. I left.

options.label: Watch the cabin a while first

text: Nobody came or went in an hour. The lamp never flickered. I'm going in.
Watched. Something watched back from the window. I left.

options.label: Climb the mast for parts instead

text: Pulled the dish feed and a box of relays. Good haul. The lamp watched me the whole time.
Ice on the rungs.

intro: A logbook on the table. Radio frequencies, times, the weather.
The last entry is today. The handwriting is mine.

text: It says I came in, read the last page, and left with the logbook.
It says that's what I'll do. I'm doing it. I don't want to.
success.memory: the logbook in the cabin in my handwriting

text: I tried to read it. The words kept sliding. I left it open.
Burned it. The lamp went out when the last page did. Took their tinned food. Ran.
success.memory: burning the logbook in the cabin

text: It wouldn't catch. Wet pages. Dry room. I left it.

options.label: Take the batteries and the lamp, leave the book

text: Lamp runs on a battery pack. Took it. The book stays. The book is not my problem.
Took the lamp. Behind me, a page turned.

intro: A department store, doors open. Mannequins in the window.
All of them facing the street.

options.label: Go in and look for clothes

text: Coats, boots, a pharmacy counter. And the mannequins. All facing the door I came in.
Went in. Came out. Something about the window. I can't say.
Walked past. Didn't look at the window.
Walked past. Their heads turned. They did. They DID.

intro: Upstairs. I came back down for the pharmacy counter.
The mannequins are on the stairs now. Facing up. Facing me.

options.label: Walk through them to the pharmacy

text: Walked between them. Didn't touch them. Filled the bag at the counter. Walked out between them.
success.memory: walking between the mannequins

text: One fell against me. Just plastic. I screamed anyway. Fell down the stairs.
Dropped to the awning, then the street. Not going back in there.
Landed badly.
Wires. Fishing line, pulleys. Someone's been moving them. Someone who wanted the place to themselves.
success.memory: the mannequins on fishing line

text: I looked too long. When I looked up, one was closer.

intro: A wedding hall. The table's still set. Eighty places. A cake, gone to stone.
One place card at the head of the table says 'RADIO'.

text: Sat. Poured an imaginary glass. Toasted you. Felt better than it should.
success.memory: the toast at the empty wedding

text: Sat. Felt like eighty people were looking at me. Got up.
Tins. A whole shelf of tins nobody wanted for a wedding.
Kitchen's been raided. Took the last two tins.
It's in my pocket. I'll give it to you.
It's in my pocket. I'll give it to you.

intro: There's a camel in the street.
I'm serious. A camel. Must be from the zoo. It's eating a hedge.

text: It ate out of my hand and followed me two blocks. Then went back to the hedge. Best day.
success.memory: the camel in the street

text: It spat at me. Fair.
It knew the way to a water main still leaking. Animals know.
success.memory: following the camel to water

text: It just walked in circles. So did I, for a while.
Left it to its hedge. Didn't believe it myself.
Left it to its hedge. Didn't believe it myself.

intro: A payphone. Ringing.
There's no line. The cable's cut. I can see the end of it.

text: Static. Then a woman, very far away: 'Is that the radio? Tell them we're still here.'
Then the dial tone. There's no line.
success.memory: the phone call on a cut line

text: Breathing. Just breathing. Then it said my name, wrong, like it read it somewhere.
It stopped ringing when I touched it. Coins, and a circuit board worth keeping.
It kept ringing while I worked. I gave up.
Let it ring. It rang until I was out of earshot. I think it stopped then.
Let it ring. It's still ringing. I can hear it from here.

intro: The botanical garden. The big glasshouse.
Half the panes are gone. It's green inside. Green and warm.

text: Lemons. Beans gone wild. Herbs. I'm going to smell like this all week.
success.memory: the glasshouse that kept growing

text: Half of it's poison or ornamental. Got some. Not much.

options.label: Lie down in the warm for a bit

text: Fell asleep under a fig tree. Woke up and forgot, for a second. That was nice.
Couldn't settle. Too quiet, too green.
Labelled envelopes in a drawer. Seeds. For the hydroponics, if anyone knows how.
Seed drawer's empty. Someone knew to come here first.

intro: A TV studio. The news desk is still there.
A tape in the deck. Label says DO NOT AIR.

text: The anchor, sweating. 'If you are hearing this, stay inside. Do not trust the... '
She looks off camera. The tape stops.
success.memory: the tape that said do not air

text: Deck's dead. I'm almost glad.
Broadcast gear. Real broadcast gear.
Pulled a cable and the lights flickered. There's no power here.

options.label: Leave the tape where it is

text: Left it. Some things weren't meant to go out.
Left it. The deck clicked as I walked out. Rewinding.

intro: A small plane. Nose-down in the park. Been here a long time.
The cockpit door is shut.

text: Empty. The pilot walked away from this. Fuel in the tank, still.
success.memory: the plane in the park

text: Not empty. Not anymore. I closed it again.
Suitcases. Someone's holiday. A good jacket, a radio, chocolate.
Picked over. Only a broken umbrella and a paperback.
Avionics. Fine work. You'll like these.
The wing shifted while I was under it.

intro: The cinema's projector is running. On its own. On a battery rig.
A beach. Waves. Nobody on it. The same thirty seconds, over and over.

text: Watched it ten times. I could almost smell it. Thank you, whoever left it on.
success.memory: the sea on the cinema screen

text: On the eleventh loop there was someone on the beach. Looking at the camera. I left.
The beach went dark. The rig's heavy and good.
Shocked myself. Took half of it.

options.label: Take the reel. Someone should keep it

text: Rolled it up careful. A beach for the bunker, if we ever have a projector.
success.memory: taking the beach reel from the cinema

text: It snapped. I took the half with the waves.

intro: A playground. One swing is moving.
No wind. The others are still.

text: Caught the chain. Cold. Under the seat, taped, a little bag. Batteries and a sweet.
When I caught it, it pulled. Just once. I let go.
It slowed, stopped. A cat jumped off the back of it. A cat. I need to sleep.
It never slowed. Not once. I'm leaving.
Went the long way. Heard it creak the whole time.
Went the long way. Heard it creak the whole time. Then heard it stop.

intro: A woman with a red cross painted on her bag. Says she's a doctor.
She'll trade medicine. For batteries. Her lamp's dying.

text: Good trade. Real antibiotics, sealed. She showed me the dates.
Half the boxes were empty. She'd gone by the time I checked.

options.label: Ask her to look at a sore spot instead

text: She checked me over, free. Said I'm in better shape than most. Said to say hi to the radio.
She said she doesn't work for free. Fair enough.
Waved. She waved back.
Waved. She waved back.

intro: A guy fixing a scooter in a garage. Smart, fast hands.
Says he'd swap parts for fuel. 'Can't ride on promises.'

text: Fuel for parts. He threw in some wire, too.
He gave me junk. I found out three streets later.

options.label: Help him fix it, for a cut

text: We got it running. He laughed like a kid. Gave me a box of what he didn't need.
I made it worse. He told me to go away, nicely.
Moved on. He didn't look up.
Moved on. He didn't look up.

intro: Three kids on a wall. Selling 'tickets' to cross their street.
One ration. Each. They're very serious about it.

text: Paid. They gave me a ticket drawn on cardboard and walked me across like an escort. Best guards in town.
success.memory: the kids who sold tickets to cross the street

text: Paid. They gave me a ticket drawn on cardboard and walked me across like an escort. Best guards in town.
failure.memory: the kids who sold tickets to cross the street

text: Went around. They booed. Fair.
Went around. They followed, booing, the whole block.
Told them I'm with the radio. They looked at each other and let me through. Saluted, too.
They didn't buy it. They threw a shoe at me.

intro: The ticket kids. They found me.
They've got something in a sack. 'For the radio. Our dad says hello.'

text: A sack of potatoes and a battery with 'RADIO' written on it. I may cry.
A sack of potatoes. A bit of a sprout on them. Still. Still.
They insisted. Then they gave me half anyway and ran off before I could argue.
They looked hurt. I took it.
